Australian XBT Ship of Opportunity gridded data collection

Since 1983, oceanographers have collected ocean temperature data from the ocean surface to approximately 800 m using Expendable BathyThermograph (XBT) instruments. The data are primarily collected from merchant vessels or research vessels along fixed transects and are freely available via the Australian Ocean Data Network (AODN). This repository contains user-friendly gridded data products created from the AODN XBT data collection, enabling easy assessment of oceanographic features such as boundary currents and Southern Ocean Antarctic fronts, decadal temperature changes and for use in model assessments.

Data were collected and made publicly available by IMOS, CSIRO, the Australian Bureau of Meteorology (BoM), Australian Geospatial-Intelligence Organisation (AGO), Scripps Institution of Oceanography, Laboratoire d’Etudes en Géophysique et Océanographie Spatiales (LEGOS), Institut de Recherche pour le Développement (IRD), Centre national de la recherche scientifique (CNRS), Institute Polaire FrancaisPaul Emile Victor (IPEV) and Atlantic Oceanographic and Meteorologic Laboratory (AOML).

Data in this file are from a single occupation of a specific transect. All bad data is excluded, the depth and temperature corrections from Cheng 2014 (2023 updates) are applied to both TEMP and DEPTH and the TEMP data is smoothed and interpolated onto a common DEPTH grid. The TEMP_uncorrected contains gridded TEMP data with DEPTH calcuated from Hanawa 1995 fall rate equation and uncorrected TEMP values.

Data may be re-used, provided that related metadata explaining the data has been reviewed by the user, and the data is appropriately acknowledged. Data, products and services from IMOS are provided "as is" without any warranty as to fitness for a particular purpose.
